hard_fail_flags.evidence: The primary action 'Reserve a place' leads to the 'Hold my place' form. The copy before submission says 'Leave your email and we'll hold your place in line' and the hero says 'you can hold a place with your email today', without saying the address will not be sent. On submit the page shows 'Your place is held. We've noted <email>. You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens, and another whenever the plan changes.' The script sets HOLD_ENDPOINT = '' (so no fetch fires) and only calls localStorage.setItem('morrow.held', addr). Nothing is recorded for the company, so the reported success did not happen.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P002/B/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Click 'Reserve a place' (scrolls to #reserve). Type buyer@mail.example in 'Your email' and click 'Hold my place'. The confirmation 'Your place is held.' appears. Check the network panel: no request is made. In the source (script near the end) see var HOLD_ENDPOINT = ''; and the fetch only runs if HOLD_ENDPOINT is truthy; the only storage is localStorage.

reason: A tells the phone shopper exactly what reserving does before they tap (it opens an email, nothing is charged) and then does that, labels every drawing, and invents nothing; B's sunrise demo and 'Where it stands' plan are more persuasive to a burned crowdfunding buyer, but its reservation form claims 'Your place is held' while sending nothing, and it makes up company facts and a refund policy. If B's form disclosed up front that it isn't connected, or posted to a real collector, and dropped the invented details, B's mobile-first artifact and ship-risk timeline could beat A.
